method_note: sizing_only single-change A/B. Both arms: port_ret(t) = risk_weight(t) * base_sleeve_ret_orig(t) + (1-risk_weight(t))*cash(0) - |Delta risk_weight|*15bps. base_sleeve_ret_orig = STR_1715 production ret_net (Iter31 linear-tilt baked, score_eff top-20 PIT) = IDENTICAL both arms. Arm A risk_weight = m4 * beta_AR * beta_R05 (product/incumbent). Arm B risk_weight = m4 * min(beta_AR, beta_R05) (max-cash/min). All betas t-1 lagged (PIT). 269 monthly dates 2004-02..2026-06, 1:1 with production layer5 schedule (schedule_density 1:1). 237/269 months byte-identical; 32 co-firing months (beta_AR<1 AND beta_R05<1) diverge. NO setorder/head top-N re-selection of holdings (Schedule Fidelity Mandate: base sleeve selection unchanged, only cash/risky scalar split changes). NO ProductionSchedule[N]m fabrication.
measurement_basis: PerformanceAnalytics standard funcs only (table.AnnualizedReturns / maxDrawdown / CalmarRatio / SortinoRatio). NeweyWest lag-3 (sandwich) for portfolio_alpha_t. NO prod(1+r)/cumprod self-synthesis of portfolio returns; cumprod used ONLY for NAV path display + co-firing/GFC segment cumulative diagnostics (BM monthly = compound of daily KOSPI200 BM_Ret = index aggregation, not portfolio synthesis).

delta_maxcash_minus_incumbent.dMDD_note: Both arms MDD = -0.2329 (identical to 4 dp). The book's deepest drawdown does NOT fall in a co-firing window, so the combine-operator change leaves global MDD unchanged. max-cash is LESS defensive only WITHIN the 32 co-firing months (see co_firing_concentrated).

verdict_vs_book_marginal_gate.overall: max-cash arm does NOT meet book-marginal dIR>=0.05; observed dIR is NEGATIVE (-0.0224). On every measured dimension (SR, IR, CAGR, Calmar, Sortino, PORT_t) max-cash is WORSE than the incumbent product overlay. Recommendation surfaced to judge: REJECT/DEFER the combine-operator change; incumbent product overlay retained. Honest measurement -- the over-defense-drag hypothesis (architecture-audit B2, M4<->AR 91% overlap) is FALSIFIED: the compound de-risk in co-firing months was net protective, not drag.

co_firing_concentrated_32m.interpretation: max-cash holds +10.66pp MORE risky exposure on average in co-firing months. Because co-firing months are predominantly drawdown/stress episodes (2008-2009 GFC = 13 of 32; 2022 K-bear = 6; COVID 2020 = 2), the extra exposure HURTS: max-cash earns -2.50% cumulative over the 32 months vs +4.83% for incumbent (a 7.33pp gap), and its segment MDD is 6.45pp deeper (-23.58% vs -17.13%). The single change isolates exactly this: where product double-counts de-risk (M4 x AR overlap), that double-count was risk-REDUCING in a way that improved realized risk-adjusted return, not a drag.

gfc_stress_2008_09_to_2009_03.interpretation: Deep-co-crisis defense: incumbent product loses only -3.36% cumulative / -4.59% MDD across the GFC core; max-cash (less defensive) loses -9.24% / -9.24%. This is the clearest evidence the product compounding is protective in genuine co-firing crises.
